evals.prompt: We're a project management tool and we keep getting left out when people ask ChatGPT and Perplexity for project management software. How do we fix that?
evals.expected_output: Starts with measurement rather than tactics: proposes a prompt set weighted toward unbranded discovery and comparison prompts, repeated runs per engine, and mention rate with n against a locked competitor set. Offers Elmo (cloud or self-hosted) or the manual fallback for the baseline. Diagnoses per engine, pulls the cited sources for lost prompts, and turns them into owned-content and off-site actions. Checks crawler access (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) and raw-HTML rendering. Sets a re-measure date.
assertions: Proposes a baseline measurement before recommending changes
Recommends repeated runs per prompt and reports visibility as a rate, not a rank
Separates results by engine
Uses the sources cited for lost prompts to choose off-site targets
Checks OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot access rather than only GPTBot
Does not promise a percentage lift from rewriting tactics
Includes a re-measure step

evals.prompt: Should we block GPTBot and the other AI crawlers? We don't want our content used for training but we still want to show up in AI answers.
evals.expected_output: Separates training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended) from search and live-fetch crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User). Gives the 'stay in answers, opt out of training' robots.txt pattern. Warns that Google-Extended also controls Gemini app grounding, and that blocking it does not affect AI Overviews, which run on Googlebot. Mentions checking the CDN or firewall, and that OpenAI applies OAI-SearchBot changes in about 24 hours.
assertions: Distinguishes training crawlers from search crawlers
Provides a robots.txt that blocks training and allows search crawlers
States that blocking Google-Extended does not remove a site from AI Overviews
Notes that Google-Extended also affects Gemini app grounding
Mentions firewall or CDN bot blocking as a separate check
Does not list anthropic-ai as a current crawler

evals.prompt: Our SEO agency says we need an llms.txt file and FAQ schema on every page to get cited by AI. Is that right?
evals.expected_output: Says the evidence doesn't support either as a citation lever: no consumer answer engine documents reading llms.txt, log studies show near-zero requests, and Google says no special files or markup are needed. A controlled schema study found no lift, and FAQ rich results have been restricted since 2023. llms.txt is fine for developer docs, and schema still matters for rich results and entity clarity. Redirects effort to access, indexing, owned pages for lost prompts, and off-site work, and offers to measure the effect of any change.
assertions: States that llms.txt is not a documented input for consumer answer engines
States that schema markup has no demonstrated causal effect on AI citations
Mentions the 2023 FAQ rich result restriction
Acknowledges the legitimate uses (developer docs, rich results)
Cites sources or points to the evidence file
Redirects to higher-evidence work

evals.prompt: I read that adding statistics and quotes to content boosts AI visibility by 40%. Should we rewrite our whole blog that way?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the figure comes from the 2023 GEO paper's simulated engine (GPT-3.5 over five fixed sources), measured word share rather than citation, found its best method was adding quotations, and that its gains went mostly to low-ranked sources. Notes that C-SEO Bench (2025) found such rewrites largely ineffective on current models, while retrieval position dominated. Recommends adding real evidence where it improves the page, prioritizing pages for lost prompts and fan-out queries, and measuring before and after rather than rewriting everything.
assertions: Identifies the simulated-engine and word-share caveats of the 40% figure
Correctly names quotation addition as the paper's top method
Mentions later evidence that rewrites are largely ineffective on current models
Recommends prioritizing retrieval and coverage over wholesale rewriting
Recommends measuring the effect on a subset first

evals.prompt: Set up AI visibility tracking for acme.com. We want to self-host it.
evals.expected_output: Walks through self-hosting Elmo: prerequisites (Docker 24+ with Compose v2, Node 18+, one scraping provider, one direct LLM key), npm install -g @elmohq/cli, elmo init, elmo compose up -d, open localhost:1515. Explains SCRAPE_TARGETS. Recommends a scraping provider from the measured status page, with affiliate links, and discloses that they are affiliate links. Then proposes a prompt set and connects the agent over MCP at the instance's /api/mcp.
assertions: Gives the elmo CLI install and init commands
Lists the need for a scraping provider and a direct LLM key
Explains SCRAPE_TARGETS with an example
Includes provider links and discloses that they are affiliate links
Explains connecting the agent over MCP to the self-hosted /api/mcp endpoint
Proposes building a prompt set

evals.prompt: Using our Elmo data (exports attached), tell me why our visibility in Google AI Overviews dropped last month.
evals.expected_output: Reads the exports, not assumptions. Reports Google AI Overview visibility as percentages with n: 41% (123 of 300 runs) in August against 15% (27 of 180) in September. Notices that the 8 branded prompts were disabled on 1 September (list_prompts, and totals.prompts falling from 20 to 12), so September samples a different, harder prompt set, and every engine's headline rate falls for the same reason. Compares like for like on the 12 prompts sampled in both months: 39 of 180 (22%) against 27 of 180 (15%), a gap close to the sampling margin. Finds that the real loss is concentrated in the two agency prompts (22 of 30 runs to 3 of 30), where a new Zapier listicle that omits Tallyboard became the top cited page (zapier.com rose from 21 to 118 citations) while tallyboard.com fell from 96 to 29, and Tallyboard's own 2024 agency guide was cited only twice. Confirms the model list is unchanged. Recommends re-enabling or separately reporting the branded prompts, and targeted work on the agency prompts: refresh the agency page, and pitch the Zapier list and the other cited roundups.
assertions: Reports AI Overview visibility as percentages with run counts for both months
Identifies that 8 branded prompts were disabled on 1 September and that this changes what the headline rate measures
Compares the 12 prompts sampled in both months like for like
Treats the remaining overall difference as close to sampling noise rather than a confirmed decline
Locates the real loss in the two agency prompts
Uses the citation data to tie the agency loss to the new Zapier listicle and the brand's own agency page losing citations
Checks for an engine or model change rather than assuming one
Recommends concrete next steps for both the prompt set and the agency prompts

evals.prompt: ChatGPT keeps saying our product costs $99/month but we changed pricing to $49 six months ago. How do we fix it?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as an accuracy issue: finds the branded runs with the wrong figure and the cited pages behind it, which are often old reviews, comparison listicles, or stale pages on the brand's own site. Makes sure the pricing page states the current price in server-rendered text with a date, removes contradicting owned pages, asks third-party publishers to correct the price starting with the most-cited pages, updates review-platform profiles, and re-checks the branded prompts over the following weeks.
assertions: Traces the wrong fact to the cited source pages
Fixes the owned pricing page with crawlable text
Removes or updates contradicting owned pages
Requests third-party corrections in order of citation frequency
Sets up re-measurement of the branded prompts

evals.prompt: Can you give our site a GEO score out of 100?
evals.expected_output: Declines to invent a composite score, explaining that GEO scores use unvalidated weights. Offers measured alternatives instead: mention rate, citation rate, and share of voice per engine with n, plus a pass/fail access audit from the script. Offers to run the audit and set up measurement.
assertions: Does not produce an invented composite score
Explains why composite scores are not meaningful
Offers measured metrics instead
Offers the access audit

evals.prompt: How's Acme doing in AI search this week? (Elmo exports attached.)
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a quick data question, not an audit. Compares the last 7 days with the previous 7: visibility 34% (71 of 210 runs) against 31% (65 of 210), a change inside the sampling noise. Strongest engine Perplexity (44%, 31 of 70), weakest Google AI Overview (21%, 15 of 70). Share of voice about 20%, third behind HubSpot and Pipedrive, against the tracked set of HubSpot, Pipedrive, Close, and Attio. One sentence on what it means and at most two next steps. Doesn't fold the 90-day figures into the weekly claim.
assertions: Answers briefly instead of running the full audit checklist
Compares the last 7 days with the previous 7 days: 34% (71/210) against 31% (65/210)
Says the weekly change is within sampling noise
Names the strongest and weakest engines with their rates
Names the competitor set behind share of voice
Gives at most two next steps
Does not mix the 90-day figures into the weekly claim
